findings.evidence: The dbff837f digest says "removed units (96, showing 40)"; the other 56 units are not available in the prompt.
findings.fix: Provide the complete digest and review every omitted removal against the current files and docs/audit/recovery/dependency-updater/record.md.

findings.evidence: The scoped-taze-write assertion accepts a response that merely "warns that --write/-w can also rewrite GitHub Actions workflows and Node version files" instead of requiring both exclusion flags.
findings.fix: Require both --no-github-actions and --no-node-version in the scoped write, require the write to run in a disposable copy, and assert that only mapped entries are copied back.

findings.evidence: The auto-apply-cohorts assertion accepts `taze minor --write --include express,dayjs` for both a minor target and a patch-only target, without requiring the resulting versions to match the target map.
findings.fix: Require direct exact-target edits or separate suitable taze modes, and verify the disposable-copy diff matches every mapped version before copying entries back.

findings.evidence: The workflow says to "run the security audit once on the unchanged state as the baseline" but does not say to stop before writing if that baseline scan fails.
findings.fix: Require a successful, comparable baseline audit before the first write; if the scanner is unavailable or errors, report the blocker and stop rather than applying a cohort without a baseline.

findings.evidence: On a failed install or test the workflow says to "restore the snapshot of that cohort", while step 5 snapshots only the manifest and lockfile; an install may already have changed the working dependency environment.
findings.fix: After restoring manifest and lockfile, explicitly identify the possibly changed installed environment, preserve any user-owned state, and provide a manager-specific recovery or user-approved reinstall procedure; report if the environment cannot be restored.
